title: TartanHacks 2026
text:
TartanHacks 2026

Presented by ScottyLabs&

TARTANHACKS is the largest Hackathon in Pittsburgh! Organized by ScottyLabs, it's a 24-hour hackathon where participants from all over the country create innovative projects. Come on over to hack, learn from our workshops and incredible speakers, and meet other hackers.

---

## This year's theme is...

MOSAIC

For 24 hours, step into a world built from fragments,floating tiles, ideas that refract and snap into place.

Nothing arrives whole; everything begins as a piece. You and your team gather scattered bits of vision, skill, and code, assembling them into something greater than any single part. Every insight becomes a tile and every teammate a new color. As the hours pass, the picture will sharpen, a Mosaic taking shape.

Enter with fragments.Leave with something whole.

---

## SCHEDULE

SPEAKER Stephen Wolfram Stephen Wolfram is the creator of Mathematica, a scientific computing platform used by thousands of engineers and scientists worldwide. He is the CEO of Wolfram Research, a software and technology consulting company that serves industry, government, and academia. Wolfram holds a PhD in physics from the California Institute of Technology and is a MacArthur Fellow. He last visited CMU over 30 years ago. --

**Think of it as the "Shark Tank" of the Atlantic Coast Conference. # Student Travel Grants

The IEEE Engineering Medicine and Biology Society (EMBS) is pleased to provide travel grants on a highly competitive basis to EMBS student members to attend EMBC. The grants will be awarded to a limited number of applicants who have a genuine need for support, and the paper quality will be taken into consideration. EMBS student membership is required at the time when the application is made. Find out more information on how to join EMBS.

The grants can only be used to cover the travel expenses for applicants to attend the approved conference. The grants, if approved, will be on a reimbursement basis following instructions given to grantees. The EMBS travel grant selection and oversight committees reserve the right to make the final decision regarding all applications.

# Kelly-Douglas Fund
**Travel Fellowships for IAP and Summer**
## 
**The power of travel**
An important dimension of the Kelly-Douglas Fund is the support for and encouragement of undergraduate education in the humanities, arts and social sciences. We believe that travel outside MIT to pursue an independent project in a HASS field, or to collaborate in a humanitarian project, can have a powerful and lasting effect on students. To this end, a portion of the Fund is reserved for Traveling Fellowships for MIT students pursuing an endeavor of their own devising either during IAP or the Summer.
**Who can apply?**
All MIT sophomores, juniors, and seniors wishing to travel during IAP or Summer are eligible to apply. Students need not belong to the School of HASS, though majors and minors in the School will be given preference.

# Travel Grant

Note: Travel funds for the Fall 2025 semester have been exhausted. We are currently accepting travel grant applications for the Spring 2026 semester.

The Virginia Tech Office of Undergraduate Research encourages students to present their research at conferences. OUR travel support program will cover expenses related to presenting at a conference. This rolling review process is designed to assist undergraduate students who have had their research or creative scholarship accepted for presentation at a regional, national or international conference. This program will provide travel funding to students who, without this support, may not be able to attend a conference to present their work. Current undergraduates from any discipline are eligible to apply for travel support.

The office will match funds you secure from other sources (such as your research mentor, department, college, student organization, student government, etc.) up to $750 for domestic travel and $1000 for international travel to support your travel, based on fund availability. Students must apply before they present at a conference. Please note that we are only able to fund one student per accepted presentation and students will only be eligible to receive travel support once per academic year. # AnitaB.org Kamala Scholars
The AnitaB.org Kamala Scholars Program empowers the next generation of innovators by providing resources, mentorship, and access to Grace Hopper Celebration.
***2026 Applications coming soon!***
Two professional women building tech.
## About the Kamala Scholars Program
The Kamala Scholars Program is a year-long opportunity made possible through the generosity of an anonymous donor, in honor of a family member, and is dedicated to opening doors and creating pathways for 3rd- and 4th-year undergraduate students pursuing technical computing fields. AnitaB.org offers many opportunities to elevate the full diaspora of our community. This particular scholarship is focused exclusively on Black and Latine students, in alignment with the donor’s wishes. Each year, we welcome 100 students into the program.
